sources.entry: MacNTop - macOS menu bar system monitor with retro CRT aesthetics.

summary.one_liner: MacNTop is a macOS menu bar system monitor that shows CPU, memory, network, disk and process stats in a popover or floating window, styled with retro CRT visual effects.
keywords: see what is using my cpu
summary.what_it_does: MacNTop lives in the macOS menu bar and shows live CPU usage per core with sparklines, memory broken into active, wired and compressed parts, and upload/download network speeds with sparklines. It also reports volume usage and disk I/O speeds, plus a top-10 process list that can be sorted by CPU or memory. The dashboard opens as a popover on left-click, or can be detached into a standalone floating window that stays on top and persists across spaces. Visual styling includes phosphor glow, scanlines and vignetting, with six selectable themes, and the chosen theme is saved in UserDefaults. The README states that all data stays local and nothing is collected or transmitted.
use_cases: monitor cpu and memory from the menu bar
watch network upload and download speed
check disk space and I/O on a Mac
find which process uses the most CPU or memory
keep a always-on-top system dashboard open
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
stack: host_processor_info / host_statistics64 / getifaddrs / statfs / proc_listallpids system APIs
notable: Retro CRT look with phosphor glow, scanline overlay and vignette effects
Six color themes including Retro Green, Amber CRT, Blue Ice, Matrix, Dracula and Light
Detachable always-on-top floating window that persists across spaces
Metrics collected through actor-based monitors using native macOS system APIs
Runs entirely locally with no data collection, per the README
caveats: Must be distributed outside the App Store because it uses restricted APIs
Process monitoring is limited to the current user's processes
Disk I/O monitoring requires IOKit access
